title: Digital Agency for Zurich: AI, Cloud, Web, Growth | 22 Signals
description: 22 Signals works with Zurich and Swiss companies on AI, cloud, data, web, apps, search, paid media, video and 3D, delivered in English with dates in writing.
h1: A digital agency for Zurich companies that also builds AI, data and cloud
intro: 22 Signals works with Zurich companies as one team for AI, automation, data, cloud, websites, apps, search, paid media, video and 3D. We are registered in London and work remotely, with visits when a project needs them. Work is delivered in English, plans come in writing within a week, and every date we agree is written down.

sections.h: What one team means in practice
p: Zurich clients tend to ask direct questions, so here are direct answers. We work with Zurich and Swiss clients remotely, plan trips for workshops, shoots and launches when they are worth it, and tell you up front which parts of a project need someone in the room. Everything else runs through shared documents, short calls and written updates.

What you get is range. Search for a digital agency, Zurich gives you plenty of studios that do one thing well: a web shop, a performance marketing team, a video house, an IT partner. 22 Signals covers technology and marketing together, so the AI tool, the data underneath it, the website it sits on and the campaign that sends people there are planned by the same people.

sections.h: A city that runs on trust
p: Zurich is Switzerland's largest city and its financial centre. Private banks, wealth managers, asset managers, global insurers and reinsurers sit within a few tram stops of each other, alongside fintechs, consultancies and law firms that serve them. Large global technology companies run major engineering sites here, and ETH Zurich turns out engineers and researchers that the whole region competes for.

Further out, the Swiss economy adds pharma and life sciences around Basel, commodity trading in Geneva, Zug and Lugano, medtech, precision manufacturing and a long list of family-owned industrial firms. The common thread is a client base that expects precision, discretion and work that holds up under audit. Loose promises do not last long here, and neither do suppliers who miss dates.

Switzerland has four national languages. Zurich speaks German, with Swiss German in daily conversation and standard German in writing. Geneva and Lausanne work in French, Ticino in Italian, and English is the working language of many banks, tech firms and international teams. A company selling across the country often needs its site, ads and support in at least two of those.

We deliver our own work in English. When you need German, French or Italian versions, we arrange localisation with specialist partners or work with your own translators, and we build the structure so each language version is set up properly for search and for people. We will not tell you our team writes Swiss German copy, because it does not.

sections.h: Swiss data rules, not EU ones by default
p: Switzerland is not in the European Union, so GDPR is not its home law. Swiss companies follow the revised Federal Act on Data Protection, the FADP, which came into force in September 2023. It covers transparency, data security, privacy by design and what happens when personal data leaves the country, and the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner oversees it.

GDPR still matters for any Swiss firm that serves customers in the EU, and so does the EU AI Act for anyone placing AI systems on the EU market. Banks and insurers add FINMA's expectations on outsourcing, operational risk and confidentiality. We are not your lawyers. We build so that your legal and compliance people can review a clear record of what data goes where, and sign it off without chasing us.

sections.h: How projects run: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
list: Talk: a 15-minute call to see whether we are the right fit. No pitch deck.
Plan: discovery and a written roadmap within 5 to 7 days, with owners, scope and dates.
Build: specialist teams do the work, and every delivery date goes in writing.
Grow: we measure what changed, report it plainly and keep improving what works.

p: Calls and reviews are booked at times that suit your team, and each one starts from a written update so the meeting is spent on decisions. Releases are planned with you in advance and written into the schedule, with a named person on our side checking the work before it reaches you.
When a visit adds real value, such as a discovery workshop with your partners, a product shoot or a launch, we include it in the scope and agree the dates with you.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe and the UAE, delivered more than 30 AI builds, broadcast more than 20 live events and managed more than $1.5M in projects. We do not publish client names. If you want to see work close to your own problem, ask on the first call and we will walk you through it.

Our best Zurich fits are established companies with a capable core team and more projects than people: a wealth manager rebuilding its client portal, an insurer automating parts of claims handling, a medtech firm launching a product in three languages, a property developer that needs renders and a sales site, a scale-up out of the ETH ecosystem that needs its product built and marketed. Ambitious founders use the same process, only faster.

faqs.q: What does a first project usually cover?
faqs.a: Most Zurich clients start with one defined piece of work, such as a website rebuild, a reporting setup or an automation for a manual process. Discovery comes first, then a written roadmap within a week with scope, owners and dates. When a workshop, shoot or launch needs us there in person, we plan the trip as part of the scope.

We deliver in English. Where you need German, French or Italian, we arrange localisation through specialist partners or work with your own translators, and we set up each language version properly for search and accessibility. Many Zurich companies already run key projects in English, so this rarely slows things down.

faqs.q: Do you follow the Swiss FADP or GDPR?
faqs.a: Both, where each applies. The revised FADP is the Swiss baseline. GDPR also applies when you serve people in the EU. We map which rules touch each system, keep data in the regions you choose and document it so your legal team can review it. Final legal sign-off stays with your advisers.

faqs.q: How are you different from a digital agency Zurich firms already use?
faqs.a: Range. Most agencies cover marketing or technology. We build AI tools, cloud systems, data pipelines, websites and apps, and we also run search, paid media, video and 3D. When one team owns all of it, a problem gets fixed instead of passed between suppliers.

faqs.q: Which Swiss industries do you know best?
faqs.a: Financial services, insurance and wealth management, professional services, technology and AI companies, healthcare and life sciences, property and manufacturing. We also work with consumer brands selling across Switzerland and into the EU.

faqs.q: How do you price work for Zurich clients?
faqs.a: After the first call, once we understand scope. The main factors are which services you need, how many systems or languages are involved, compliance requirements and whether the work is a project or ongoing. Third-party costs such as licences and ad spend are paid by you directly.

faqs.q: How quickly can a project start?
faqs.a: The first call can usually happen within days. Discovery and a written roadmap take 5 to 7 days after that. Build dates are agreed in writing once the roadmap is approved, and you hear early if anything puts one at risk.
